text:
jun: Hey team — PR #21387 is blocked from merging. CI shows an intermittent failure in TelemetryTest.test_startup_count on windows-integ-4. It passes locally for me. Anyone seen this recently?

sophia: Ugh, saw that earlier in another PR. Looks nondeterministic — sometimes timing-related. Failing assert: expected 5, got 4.

jun: here's the failing snippet from the job logs:
```
AssertionError: expected 5 != 4
  File "/workspace/tests/test_telemetry.py", line 78, in test_startup_count
    assert metrics.startup_count == 5
  Waited 3.2s for metrics flush
```

erin: Repro attempted with pytest -k TelemetryTest on a windows runner?

jun: I re-ran the job twice via Buildkite but only reproduced once.

matt: @oncall-sre can you help bisect whether this is a recent change or an infra flake? Could be the telemetry agent occasionally dropping one event under load.

oncall-sre: I'll pick it up. Quick question — does the test rely on real timers or any sleep windows that could be flaky under CI load?

jun: It uses a short wait loop to poll the in-memory metrics export. There is a TODO to replace with an event-driven flush.

ci-bot: buildkite: re-run scheduled (2/3) — Job: windows-integ-4 — triggered by jun

erin: If we can't immediately root cause, options: 1) targeted rerun + merge on green, 2) quarantine the test behind @flaky_tests, or 3) add a small backoff in test + a comment to revert. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

matt: I'd prefer targeted rerun + a quick bisect. If we hit it on master we should open an infra ticket. If only on PRs, maybe test timing.

jun: I'll do a focused bisect (bisect range: last green commit 9f2a -> head). Will report back in this thread.

oncall-sre: FYI I kicked an agent reboot on windows-integ-4 to rule out transient host issues.

sophia: If you end up needing to bypass to keep release moving, I'm ok with a temporary skip on windows with a link to this thread and a revert issue. Prefer not to change production code for tests.

jun: Action items: 1) I will bisect and post results here within the hour. 2) @matt please approve a targeted rerun if bisect inconclusive. 3) @sophia please sign off on temporary skip if the bisect pins it to CI infra.

matt: ACK. If bisect shows test landed in our PR surface, we'll add a deterministic wait and ask for quick review.

jun: Update 11m: bisect narrowed failure to commit 0b7c3 (telemetry exporter change). Reproduced once at that commit. Filing PR to add a slightly longer flush wait + a TODO to rework to event-driven flush: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-infra/pull/21390

erin: Nice, thanks. Can you also add a test comment referencing CI job id and this thread? Makes future triage easier.

jun: Will do. Filing follow-up ticket for the event-driven fix and linking it.

matt: Once the quick-fix PR is up, ping me for a review and I'll try to approve within the hour so we can unblock the merge window. :+1:

ci-bot: buildkite: PR #21390 — windows-integ-4 targeted run queued by jun

jun: Thanks everyone — keeping this thread updated.
